name: Highperch Wyvern Egg
summary: At Highperch, Horde trainees seek wyvern eggs to raise as mounts. The nests lie above the mesas of Thousand Needles.

sections.title: Nests on the Mesa
sections.body: Highperch gives native wyverns a place to roost and raise their young above Thousand Needles. Steep paths wind up the canyon walls to the nesting grounds, where adult wyverns guard their nests. Within sturdy, warm shells, hatchlings wait to face Kalimdor's harsh skies.

sections.title: Raising New Wind Riders
sections.body: The Horde needs more trained wyverns for its courier and scouting networks across Kalimdor. At Freewind Post, trainees such as the tauren Elu seek intact eggs from wild nests. They raise the hatchlings from the shell, hoping to form the bond that makes a trustworthy mount for a wind rider.

faq.answer: The eggs lie in nests across Highperch, a mesa along the western rock walls of Thousand Needles. A path climbs there from the canyon floor.

faq.q: Why does the Horde collect wild wyvern eggs?
aliases: what are the eggs used for
faq.answer: The Horde's wind rider ranks are growing, and trained wyverns are in short supply. Trainees such as Elu gather eggs and raise the hatchlings from birth for aerial duty.

faq.q: Are the parent wyverns hostile to egg gatherers?
faq.answer: Yes. Wild wyverns fiercely guard their nests and attack intruders who trespass on Highperch to disturb their clutches.

faq.q: Who accepts these eggs in Freewind Post?
faq.answer: Elu, an aspiring wind rider stationed at Freewind Post, collects eggs to begin training a mount of his own.

angles.text: As a member of the Horde, you know reliable air travel keeps communication and military readiness across Kalimdor's vast territories. Fresh wyverns matter to both.
As a hunter, you must read the fierce predators guarding Highperch. Adult wyverns defend their nests with claws and venomous stingers.
